h1: Beauty Video Templates for Skincare Ads
lead: Beauty video templates can start from the cleanser already on your sink. Upload that pump photo and an AI actor can walk through the routine.
steps_h2: How to Make a Beauty Ad in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: One cleanser photo becomes a sink-side clip you can post. The pump and the label stay in frame.

steps.d: Add a clear photo of the ivory cleanser pump, with the cap and label included. You get a file that still shows that same bottle.
Ask for one pump at a bright sink, with foam on the fingertips. You get a 9:16 clip in 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.
Set the voice, then add the shade name in captions and download. You get a cleanser clip with nothing stamped on it.

faq.q: What does a beauty video template include?
faq.a: It is a sink-side ad shape for a cleanser you already photographed. An AI actor, a voice, and a script come with that shape. You are not building the morning routine from a blank page.

faq.q: How does a beauty video template work?
faq.a: Add the cream photo, name the jar in the line you would say, and pick 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. A product link can supply the first draft. Your own software can start that job through the API.

faq.q: Why use this beauty template instead of booking a creator?
faq.a: You can still publish the launch ad when your usual creator is booked. You can change the shade name and cut a second mascara version while that booking stays out.

faq.q: Who should use a beauty template?
faq.a: Someone selling a shampoo who already has the bottle photo. A small beauty team and an agency making a client file fit the same way. Anyone on screen is an AI avatar. You can pick from 53 AI actors.

faq.q: Can I make the clip with no editing practice?
faq.a: Yes. One clear lip-balm photo is the start. Shorten a long caption in the editor, and a song from the music library can sit under the voice.

faq.q: Is this template only for skincare?
faq.a: This template is for beauty and personal care: a routine, a texture, or a short review. The wider library also has clothing, food, fitness, pets, and home. Open another template when the product is not a beauty item.

faq.q: Can I bring photos and clips I already own?
faq.a: Yes. Bring the toner photo you shot on the shelf, plus a short clip if you filmed the texture yourself and you have the rights. The toner can be the only subject in the frame.

faq.q: Where do these beauty clips get posted?
faq.a: Choose the shape for the place you already post. A tall 9:16 suits TikTok, a square 1:1 suits a Facebook feed, and 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 cover the other slots. Instagram, YouTube, and LinkedIn can take the file you download, or you can send it from AIVideosUGC.

faq.q: What does a beauty clip cost?
faq.a: A clip spends 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. You see that number first. If it fails, those credits come back. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: Can the file run in paid ads and client work?
faq.a: Yes. A blush clip can run as a paid ad or go to a client as a delivery. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: Why use a beauty template instead of building a scene?
faq.a: The sink, the pace, and the place the cleanser sits are already decided. You spend the time on the shade name, then post.
